ratings.reviewer_notes: A small-molecule inhibitor interfered with JAK2/STAT2/STAT3 signaling and inhibited myogenic differentiation, but the compound is not named in the abstract.
Directly shows that the JAK2 inhibitor AG490 reduces muscle STAT3 phosphorylation and attenuates sepsis-induced tibialis anterior atrophy; IL-6 also activates the pathway in myotubes.
Pharmacological STAT3 inhibition ameliorated soleus muscle loss in VDR-null mice, but the STAT3 inhibitor is not identified in the abstract.

An Alk5 inhibitor plus oxytocin restored exercise-associated proteomic abnormalities involving JAK/STAT among several pathways in aged skeletal muscle, but pathway-specific modulation by either agent is not clearly isolated.
Direct skeletal-muscle evidence that SGI-1252 reduces gastrocnemius STAT3 phosphorylation and alters satellite-cell content and myogenic differentiation.
IFN-gamma induced JAK1/2-associated muscle stem-cell dysfunction, while ruxolitinib blocked IFN-gamma responses in vitro and improved myofiber size and atrophy biomarkers in vivo.
Review-level context linking macrophage-derived cytokines such as IL-6 to JAK-STAT activation and muscle atrophy; specific chemical modulation evidence is not detailed.
Describes endogenous JAK/STAT phosphorylation during human myoblast proliferation and differentiation without testing a chemical modulator.
Directly demonstrates that exogenous IL-6 activates JAK/STAT-dependent mitochondrial responses in myotubes; MitoQ partly attenuates IL-6-induced STAT3 activation.
Direct human skeletal-muscle intervention showing that the JAK inhibitor tofacitinib increases single-fiber contractile force and alters associated molecular signaling.
IFN-gamma activates JAK/STAT1-associated wasting in engineered human skeletal muscle, and JAK/STAT inhibitors fully prevent the induced myopathy, although the inhibitors are unnamed.
Review-level discussion identifies JAK-STAT signaling as a therapeutic target in cancer cachexia-associated skeletal muscle atrophy but names no relevant modulating chemical in the abstract.
Directly tests C188-9, showing STAT3 pathway suppression and reduced skeletal muscle wasting in septic mice and reduced atrophy in C2C12 myotubes.
Direct evidence that scutellarein inhibits JAK kinases/JAK-STAT activation and mitigates muscle atrophy in skeletal muscle cell systems and two cancer-cachexia mouse models.
Broad review of JAK/STAT signaling across obesity and diabetes organs; the abstract provides no specific chemical modulation evidence in skeletal muscle.
Directly shows that sulforaphane increases JAK2/STAT3 pathway activity during muscle regeneration, with a JAK2 inhibitor blocking sulforaphane-induced Prl2c2 transcription and myoblast proliferation.
Review-level evidence concerning IL-6/IL-6R/JAK/STAT signaling in skeletal muscle regeneration and wasting, including proposed IL-6R antibodies and kinase inhibitors.
Skeletal muscle-focused review discussing IL-6 activation and pharmacological or epigenetic modulation of JAK/STAT, without identifying specific chemicals in the abstract.
Directly reports that JAK2/STAT3 inhibition alters expansion and maturation of human iPSC-derived myogenic progenitors, but the chemical inhibitor is not identified.
Direct evidence that the STAT3 inhibitor C188-9 reduces STAT3 activation and prevents burn-induced skeletal muscle and C2C12 myotube wasting.
Concerns genomic diagnosis of primary atopic disorders and provides no skeletal-muscle JAK/STAT modulation evidence.
Review-level mechanistic context on cytokine-activated JAK/STAT signaling in myogenic differentiation, but no specific chemical modulator is identified.
Metyrapone was administered during sleep deprivation and muscle p-STAT3/IL-6 were measured, but the abstract does not clearly establish that metyrapone specifically modulated JAK/STAT signaling.
